headline: HPE has launched its first four ProLiant Gen13 servers, all using AMD's newest server processors.
score_reason: Pool 6 kept: an official HPE launch, reported with the product detail from HPE's release.
importance_line: What changed: IT and data-centre teams at large companies get new AMD-based servers for AI and engineering work, with the DL525 shipping first; HPE's claim of up to twice the compute performance does not name the system it was compared with, so it is HPE's own figure.
summary: StorageReview reports that HPE, the computer maker, has launched its first four ProLiant Gen13 servers, all running AMD's sixth-generation EPYC server processors, including an eight-GPU DL585a and a single-processor DL525 that ships first. HPE aims them at agentic AI (AI systems that carry out multi-step tasks) and engineering simulation, and its release says the wider Gen13 range will reach mainstream enterprise servers later, with no date given.
notes: Chunk source Data Center Dynamics blocked (403). Read on StorageReview, which reports HPE's launch with its QuickSpecs and a briefing call. Credit goes to StorageReview as the outlet read; the DCD headline is the same launch.
